page.layout: One page of running text: a continuous Latin commentary with Greek words. Running head at the top with the page number at top left. Below the text: a centred heading "Ad caput ἀπονοίας." followed by a centred reference "Pap. 19." and one paragraph with a large initial. No marginal notes and no footnotes.

main_text.p: vitij huius simplicitate, quàm illa iactatione peruersi, si abundans opibus pauperem se neget, nobilis obseruans, & potens infirmum, aut si se dissertus imperitum plane infantem vocet. Παλαιστρᾶν[?] certum est de loco hic esse accipiendum, vt Pars in gramineis exercet membra palaestris. Est autem commune poëtis, philosophis, sophistis, hoplomachis, harmonicis, atque aliis item, vt τὰ μελέται[?], sic etiam τὸ ἐπιδεικνύσθαι[?] habent enim quique eorum suas ἐπιδείξεις & exercitationes: quod notum est ex Græcis scriptoribus. Ὁπλομάχοι sunt, qui sub campidoctore veris armis certare discunt, aut ipsi qui docent: puto enim vtrunque hac voce significari. vide Platonem in Lachete. At vulgò inuentus non veris armis se exercebat: sed tudibus, aut pilis præpilatis, quæ dicuntur Græcis ἐσφαιρωμένα ἀκόντια. Xenophon libro secundo Ἀναβάσεως de Phalino quodam ita scribens, [illegible, ~20 letters] videtur innuere hoplomachos ea ætate fuisse appellatos, etiam eos qui tacti-ci Græcis proprie dicuntur. vide Vegetium.
main_text.head: Ad caput ἀπονοίας.
main_text.p: Ἡ δὲ ἀπόνοια ἐστιν [illegible, ~12 letters] τῶν ἔργων καὶ λό-γων. ] Definitio ista ἀπονοίας parum plena est nam cum discrimen latum sit inter ἀναιδωλίαν[?], de qua infrà est integrum caput, & ἀπὸ οἴας[?] nihil videtur in hac definitione, quod non conueniat etiam τῇ ἀναιδωλίᾳ. quid enim pudor aliud est quàm vi-

page.notes: Greek readings marked [?] or illegible are doubtful: the line "scribens, ..." (p. 172, line 18) is mostly unreadable on the scan, and the opening of the Greek in the large-initial paragraph is faint. The Greek words Παλαιστρᾶν, τὰ μελέται, τὸ ἐπιδεικνύσθαι, ἀναιδωλίαν and ἀπὸ οἴας are best readings. The paragraph ends mid-line with "vi-" and continues on the next page with "tiosæ". No catchword and no signature are printed.
